nodes.label: Whisper domain-hint prompt
nodes.rationale: Video/audio can't be read directly, so instead of a separate API call, the agent (already a language model) writes a one-sentence domain hint itself from existing god-node labels and passes it to Whisper as GRAPHIFY_WHISPER_PROMPT to improve transcription accuracy.

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS if unsure); never skip the corpus-size warning; always show token cost; never hide cohesion scores behind symbols; never run HTML viz on a graph with more than 5,000 nodes without warning the user. Keeps the audit trail honest and prevents silent quality loss.

nodes.label: Interpreter guard for subcommands
nodes.rationale: Before running --update, --cluster-only, query, path, explain, or add, verify graphify-out/.graphify_python exists and re-resolve the interpreter if missing (e.g. the user deleted graphify-out/), so subcommands don't fail on a stale cached interpreter path.

nodes.label: Confidence score rubric
nodes.rationale: INFERRED edges must pick exactly one discrete value from {0.95, 0.85, 0.75, 0.65, 0.55} rather than a continuous range, because production data showed scores collapsing bimodally to 0.5 and 0.85+ when given free-range guidance; discrete rubrics are followed more faithfully by models. If nothing fits, mark AMBIGUOUS instead of picking below 0.4.

nodes.label: Node ID format rule
nodes.rationale: IDs must be {stem}_{entity} using the full repo-relative path with every directory segment kept (not just the immediate parent), so same-named files in different directories don't collapse into orphan ghost-duplicate nodes; this must match the AST extractor's ID format exactly. Projects built under the old immediate-parent format need `graphify extract --force` to rebuild cleanly.

nodes.label: Step 0: Constrained query expansion
nodes.rationale: The query CLI matches nodes via case-folded substring + IDF with no stemming, synonyms, or cross-language matching, so a wording mismatch between the user's question and the graph's own label vocabulary collapses the answer to noise. Fixing this requires expanding the query against the actual extracted node-label vocabulary first, never inventing tokens, and stopping if no vocab tokens match rather than fabricating a search.
